To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a new mechanism of neurodegeneration, namely dysfunctional RBPs, in MS.
neuronal RNA‐binding protein (RBP) dysfunction is associated with neurodegeneration in multiple sclerosis ( MS ).

we identified evidence of altered RBP expression, mislocalization, stress granule assembly, and altered RNA processing in MS cortical neurons, which is consistent with the hypothesis that dysfunctional RBPs contribute to the pathogenesis of neuronal dysfunction in MS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how RNA‐binding proteins are involved in neurodegeneration in multiple sclerosis.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis and other neurological disorders.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie neuronal dysfunction in MS and other neurological diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supports the hypothesis that RBP dysfunction in MS is associated with neurodegeneration.
the evidence is consistent with the notion that RBP dysfunction is a common feature of neurodegeneration across neurodegenerative diseases.
the evidence is insufficient to support or refute the hypothesis that neuronal RNA‐binding protein function is altered in the MS cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is evidence of RBP mislocalization from the nucleus to the cytoplasm in MS cortical neurons and that there is a strong association of the presence of stress granules and the presence of neurodegeneration.
we have found evidence for altered RBP function and RNA metabolism in the brains of people with MS.
there is widespread RBP dysfunction in the MS brain, which is likely to contribute to the pathogenesis of MS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found that there is a loss of RBPs in the cytoplasm of MS neurons, and we also found a loss of RBMs, which are a class of RNA‐binding motifs that are found in many RBPs.
we found evidence of RBP function in cortical neurons in the cortex.
there is widespread evidence of RBP dysregulation in MS cortex.
